Introduction to Howard County, Missouri and This Tax Sale Guide

Howard County sits in central Missouri along the Missouri River. The county seat is Fayette. It is a small county with farmland, historic towns, and steady property ownership records.

Many investors study counties like this because property prices are modest and competition stays manageable. This guide explains how Howard County handles delinquent property tax sales. It covers the schedule, auction process, redemption rules, and investor requirements. The goal is to help new and experienced investors understand how the local tax certificate sale works and how to prepare before bidding.

What Is Howard County’s Tax Lien Investing System?

Missouri uses a tax lien certificate system. Howard County follows this model. When property owners fail to pay taxes, the county sells a tax lien certificate at a public auction.

The winning bidder pays the unpaid taxes and fees. In return, the investor receives a certificate that earns interest. The owner can redeem the property by paying the delinquent taxes plus interest.

If the owner does not redeem within the allowed time, the investor may begin steps toward ownership. This structure makes Missouri tax sales a popular option for investors who want income with real estate security.

Important Details About Howard County Tax Sales

Key Takeaways
  • Howard County, Missouri, offers a tax lien certificate system where investors buy certificates for unpaid taxes at annual auctions.
  • The auction typically occurs on the fourth Monday in August and allows bidders to earn interest on invested amounts.
  • Investors benefit from lower property prices and less competition, making Howard County ideal for tax lien investing.
  • Due diligence is crucial; investors must research properties and potential issues before bidding to avoid costly mistakes.
  • Howard County’s stable rural economy and regular auction schedule attract both local and foreign investors.

Recent example: Public notices indicate recent auctions scheduled around late August, which follows the traditional fourth Monday schedule used by many Missouri counties.

Fun Facts About Howard County

  • Population is a little over 10,000 residents.
  • The county was founded in 1816 and is one of the oldest counties in Missouri.
  • Fayette is home to Central Methodist University.
  • Agriculture drives much of the local economy, especially corn and soybean farming.
  • Median home value is about $134,900, which keeps entry costs low for investors.

Howard County has a long history tied to river trade and farming. Many properties are rural parcels or small town homes. This creates a mix of tax sale opportunities each year.

Auction Process for Howard County Tax Lien Sales

Howard County runs a public auction for delinquent tax liens. The county collector conducts the sale at the courthouse. Properties with unpaid taxes are listed and offered one by one.

Missouri law governs how the bidding process works. The winning bidder pays the taxes owed and receives a certificate of purchase.

Most counties publish the list of delinquent properties before the sale so investors can research them.

How the Auction Works

Typical tax lien auction process

  • The county publishes a delinquent property list before the sale.
  • Investors review parcels and conduct research.
  • The auction begins at the courthouse at about 10:00 AM Central Time.
  • Each property is announced by parcel number and owner name.
  • Bidding begins at the total delinquent taxes, interest, and fees.
  • Investors compete by offering a higher premium amount.
  • The highest bidder wins the tax lien certificate.
  • Payment is usually due immediately after the auction.
  • The collector issues a certificate of purchase to the winning bidder.

Buyers must also sign an affidavit confirming they are not delinquent on Missouri taxes before bidding.

Maximum Potential Returns and Expected Returns on Howard County Tax Lien Certificates

Missouri tax lien certificates offer interest that accrues during the redemption period. The rate can reach about 10 percent annually depending on the county and sale structure.

If the property owner redeems the lien, the investor receives:

  • The amount paid for the lien
  • Interest earned during the holding period
  • Any approved fees

Many investors treat these certificates as income investments. The return depends on how quickly the property owner redeems the taxes.

If redemption does not occur, the investor may move forward with legal steps that can lead to a tax deed. That outcome can produce a property acquisition below market value.

Open to All Investors and Foreign Participation

Missouri tax lien sales are generally open to public bidders. Local investors, out of state buyers, and international investors can participate.

There is no residency requirement for purchasing tax lien certificates in Missouri. However, investors must follow state rules and complete required paperwork.

Typical requirements include:

  • Signing an affidavit confirming no delinquent Missouri taxes
  • Paying the winning bid amount at the sale
  • Following redemption and notice procedures

International investors sometimes participate through U.S. entities or investment groups. Many counties see participation from buyers across several states.

Importance of Due Diligence in Howard County Tax Lien Investing

Tax lien investing works best when buyers research each property before bidding.

Even though the lien is backed by real estate, problems can still arise. Careful research helps investors avoid costly surprises.

What Due Diligence Entails

  • Study the delinquent tax list published by the county
  • Check property location and access
  • Review zoning and land use rules
  • Inspect satellite images or visit the property
  • Check other liens or legal issues
  • Estimate market value of the property

Risks of Skipping Due Diligence

  • Property may have environmental issues
  • Land may be landlocked or unusable
  • Buildings may be abandoned or unsafe
  • Additional liens could reduce profit
  • Legal steps after redemption may cost money

Smart investors treat tax lien purchases like real estate investments.

Conclusion

Howard County offers a classic Missouri tax lien investment opportunity. The county runs its annual delinquent tax certificate sale on the fourth Monday in August at the courthouse in Fayette.

Investors purchase liens on properties with unpaid taxes. The investment earns interest during the redemption period. If the owner pays the debt, the investor receives the principal and interest.

Counties like Howard attract investors because property values remain affordable and auctions follow a clear schedule.

Even so, success depends on preparation. Investors should review property lists, inspect locations, and study Missouri tax law before bidding.

Careful research and disciplined bidding help turn tax lien certificates into a steady income strategy.

Pro Tips for Investing in Howard County Tax Liens

  • Visit Fayette before the auction. Seeing neighborhoods helps evaluate property quality.
  • Study farmland parcels carefully. Agricultural land often holds strong resale value.
  • Check Missouri River floodplain maps before bidding.
  • Watch county notice publications for updated tax sale lists.
  • Track nearby Columbia real estate trends since regional growth can affect property demand.

FAQs About Howard County Tax Lien Certificates

Can I renovate the property after buying a tax lien?

No. You must wait until ownership rights transfer through the legal process.

Do tax liens remove other debts on the property?

Some liens may remain. Title research helps determine this.

What happens if the property is occupied?

You cannot remove occupants unless you obtain legal ownership later.

Can tax lien purchases be financed?

Most auctions require full payment immediately. Financing is uncommon.

Do investors need to file a quiet title action later?

Yes. Investors usually file quiet title actions before selling the property after obtaining a deed.
